scope: Original sound set for the asena-stars slot: base / idle / feature ("Ergenekon") themes, steppe-night ambience, free-spins intro, retrigger, feature outro, total-win fanfare, win tiers 1–4 + max (heads, count-up beds, tier-ups, landings), 6 multiplier callout classes, the constellation signature (one star per lighting event of the art plan, a rising motif per template, six template ignitions, the synthesized wolf howl), column landings, cluster highlight and burst into stars by symbol, fall, wolf walk paws and star trail, moon landings 1–6 + tease and trigger, Ergenekon map pieces, the iron mountain cracking at ×2/×3/×5, +5 spins, UI effects, wordless placeholders for the sky voice and a 29-line recorded voice-bank slot. Presentation only; nothing reads or changes a result.
originality: All music and effects are original note data and code synthesis (lib/slot-audio/scores/asena.ts, sfx/asena.ts, synth/asena.ts; ney, choir, bass, sparkles, whoosh, riser and the vox placeholder from the shared kit). No samples, no recordings, no third-party melodies or motifs; no existing game, film or song imitated; the wolf howl is a vocal-formant synth, not a sampled wolf. Instruments are synthesized approximations (kopuz/dombra-like Karplus-Strong lute, kıl-kopuz-like bowed fiddle, throat-singing-inspired overtone drone, kam davulu with pendants, hoofbeats, forge anvil, star bells, aurora pad, steppe wind/crickets/fire). Only the generic three-stroke gallop figure of steppe lute music is used.

musicDirection.base: E Hüseyni (E F# G A B C# D; dominant B, the natural sixth C#) on the Central-Asian anhemitonic pentatonic E G A B D; 80 BPM, 42 s loop; vast, slow, nocturnal; a throat-singing drone on E whose overtone whistle walks harmonics 6–16 (B, ~D, E, F#, B, E); a C natural (Kürdi shadow) in the B section.
musicDirection.feature: "Ergenekon": B Kürdi (B C D E F# G A, the C→B cadence) for the iron mountain and the forge, opening to E Hüseyni (the C# returns) when the people ride out; 12/8 gallop at 100 dotted-quarter BPM, hoofbeats three per beat with the third accented, kargyraa drone on B, khoomei on E.
musicDirection.celebrations: Major pentatonic daylight (Kün Ana) of the tier key, 120 BPM: Büyük E → Mega F# → Süper G# → Efsane B → Azami C#, hoofbeat triplets from Mega up.
musicDirection.signature: The "Asena call" (E–G–B–D → E) opens the base hook and is the Kurt Başı constellation motif; every template has its own rising motif on the E pentatonic (hilal B D E · yay E G A → E6 · at B D E G A B · kartal E4 B4 B5 E6 · hayat-agaci E4 A4 D5 G5 B5 · kurt-basi E G B D E), nodes that light together ring as chords, then the template ignition bloom and the howl (great howl for Kurt Başı).
musicDirection.otherGames: Ebru G Rast / A Uşşak / Hüzzam, Tarhun A/D Hicaz, Cezeri C Nikriz / Çargah: no makam shared.

Constellations, escalation and runtime chain through the real bus graph (buildBusGraph) at the default mix. Lab page: next dev :3311 /lab/audio?game=asena.

constellation.note: All six templates in order (hilal, yay, at, kartal, hayat-agaci, kurt-basi; transforms 0..5) from components/asena/geometry.ts asenaConstellationPlan(…, 1400 ms), scheduled exactly as asena-sound.ts does (node clips at motif pitch, ignition at the plan end, howl 0.16 s later; TRACE_GAIN node 0.55, ignite 0.7, howl 0.75), with the scene ducked by 3 + 0.3 × multiplier dB.

music.about: E Hüseyni (E F# G A B C# D) on the E minor pentatonic, 80 BPM, 14-bar seamless loop (42 s). A: the "Asena call" hook (E–G–B–D → E, then the Hüseyni fall G–F#–E) on a kopuz/dombra-like lute with its drone string and dombra tremolo, a star bell on every hook bar, a throat-singing drone on E whose overtone whistle walks the drone's harmonics, one kam davulu stroke per bar · A': the kıl-kopuz-like bowed fiddle sings the low answer with the natural sixth C#, kopuz ostinato, soft bass · B: the sky opens — ney over an aurora pad, star bells on the changes, the drum heartbeat, a C natural (the Kürdi shadow) in the last bar · C: breakdown on the deep kargyraa drone with twinkling stars, a kopuz turn into the hook.

E Hüseyni, 80 BPM, 8-bar loop (24 s): a throat-singing drone on E with its overtone whistle, the Asena call hook on crystalline star bells, the kıl kopuz answer far below, an aurora pad breathing E–B and a slow kam davulu heartbeat; no lute.

"Ergenekon": 12/8 gallop at 100 dotted-quarter BPM, 16-bar loop (38.4 s). A (B Kürdi, the iron mountain): the kıl-kopuz-like fiddle leads low and wild, the kopuz doubles above, kopuz gallop strums, hoofbeats (three per beat, the third accented), kam davulu on 1 and 3 with its pendants on 2 and 4, the forge anvil, a kargyraa drone on B, the Kürdi C→B cadence · B (E Hüseyni, the people ride out): ney and a wordless female choir sing the opened sky up to E6 with the C# returning, aurora pad, star bells on the downbeats, the khoomei whistle on E, a riser and a kopuz pickup back into A.

Ambience, 24 s seamless loop: a steppe night — wind over open grass with slow far gusts, a faint whistle wandering through the grass, two distant crickets and a far camp fire (low flame roar and sparse crackles); no tempo-bound material.

Free-spins intro ("the sky gate opens"), 100 BPM: star bells cascade up the E pentatonic over two octaves while the kıl kopuz swells from B2 to B3, a choir swell, a kam davulu roll into a deep stroke with its pendants, then a B power-chord kopuz strum with a kargyraa drone on B on beat 3; the feature theme enters at beat 5 (3.0 s).

Retrigger (+3), B Kürdi/E pentatonic, 100 BPM, 1 bar: a 32nd-note star-bell and kopuz flourish B–D–E–F#–A–B up to B5, a bowed B3 with dombra tremolo, a kam davulu stroke with its pendants and a sparkle; ends at beat 3 (1.8 s) and rings over the feature theme.

Feature outro ("out of Ergenekon"), E Hüseyni, 80 BPM: C – D | Em with a kıl kopuz phrase B–A–G–F#–G–F# falling to E, kopuz strums, the aurora pad and the choir, a last star bell on E6, the throat drone on E; the base theme may return at beat 6 (4.5 s).

Total-win fanfare, E major pentatonic, 120 BPM, 4 s: E – C#m – A | B – E. A festive kopuz flourish with the kıl kopuz doubling, kopuz strums, aurora pad, choir on the final E with star bells, kam davulu with its pendants, hoofbeat triplets and a star shower.

Big win tier 1 (Büyük), E major pentatonic, 120 BPM, 2 bars (4 s): a kopuz climb with dombra tremolo on the long notes over a 16th kopuz ostinato, the kıl kopuz an octave below, aurora pad, the throat drone on the tonic, kam davulu; it lands on a held tonic with star bells, the drum's pendants and a star shower.

Big win tier 2 (Mega), F# major pentatonic, 120 BPM, 2 bars (4 s): a kopuz climb with dombra tremolo on the long notes over a 16th kopuz ostinato, the kıl kopuz an octave below, aurora pad, wordless choir, hoofbeat triplets, the throat drone on the tonic, kam davulu; it lands on a held tonic with star bells, the drum's pendants and a star shower.

Big win tier 3 (Süper), G# major pentatonic, 120 BPM, 3 bars (6 s): a kopuz climb with dombra tremolo on the long notes over a 16th kopuz ostinato, the kıl kopuz an octave below, aurora pad, wordless choir, hoofbeat triplets, the throat drone on the tonic, kam davulu, a riser and double-time drum; it lands on a held tonic with star bells, the drum's pendants and a star shower.

Big win tier 4 (Efsane), B major pentatonic, 120 BPM, 3 bars (6 s): I – IV | ii – V | I. Kopuz lead with tremolo, the kıl kopuz doubling an octave below, full choir, aurora pad, throat drone, star bells on every downbeat, hoofbeat triplets, a kam davulu roll into the last bar and two star showers.

Max win, C# (top of the key ladder), 120 BPM, 3 bars (6 s): IV – V – bVII – I (F# – G# – B – C#) with kopuz and kıl kopuz in octaves, dombra tremolo, full choir and aurora, throat drone, star bells climbing, a 16th kopuz ostinato, a kopuz strum, double-time kam davulu with a roll and its pendants, hoofbeat triplets and the biggest star shower.
Count-up bed tier 1: I – bVII – IV – I/V in E major at 120 BPM, 4-bar seamless loop (8 s); kopuz 16ths, throat drone, bass, kam davulu pulse.
Count-up bed tier 2: I – bVII – IV – I/V in F# major at 120 BPM, 4-bar seamless loop (8 s); kopuz 16ths, throat drone, bass, kam davulu pulse + drum groove, aurora pad, pendants.

Count-up bed tier 3: I – bVII – IV – I/V in G# major at 120 BPM, 4-bar seamless loop (8 s); kopuz 16ths, throat drone, bass, kam davulu pulse + drum groove, aurora pad, pendants + kopuz lead and hoofbeat triplets.

Count-up bed tier 4: I – bVII – IV – I/V in B major at 120 BPM, 4-bar seamless loop (8 s); kopuz 16ths, throat drone, bass, kam davulu pulse + drum groove, aurora pad, pendants + kopuz lead and hoofbeat triplets + choir, star bells, deep strokes.

Count-up bed max win: I – bVII – IV – I/V in C# major at 120 BPM, 4-bar seamless loop (8 s); kopuz 16ths, throat drone, bass, kam davulu pulse + drum groove, aurora pad, pendants + kopuz lead and hoofbeat triplets + choir, star bells, deep strokes + the kıl kopuz an octave below and a star shimmer.

escalation.note: Büyük → Mega → Süper → Efsane → max with count-up ticks; tier-up hits on the 120 BPM grid (planTierUp), landing at 22.3 s.

loadTiming.note: Core = base theme + base-game effects (land, burst s/m, fall, the three star-node clips, the hilal/yay/at/kartal ignitions, the howl, paws, trail, UI) rendered in parallel. The Hayat Ağacı and Kurt Başı ignitions, the large burst, the great howl, moons, Ergenekon and the celebration group follow lazily; until then the Kartal ignition (a whole tone lower), the medium burst, the ordinary howl or the live fallback voice stand in.

limitations: Nobody has listened to this set: the author cannot hear. Owner listening acceptance is required (WAV per asset; asena-constellations.wav is the signature, asena-escalation-max.wav the full climb).

Instruments are synthesized approximations, not recordings; kopuz, kıl kopuz, throat singing and the howl may read as "synth" on good speakers. Makam colours are 12-TET approximations (no quarter tones); the khoomei whistle uses natural harmonics, so its 7th harmonic is ~31 cents flat of D (intended).

Vocal callouts are wordless synthetic placeholders; the 29 recorded lines (ASENA_VOICE_TEXT, wise female sky voice) plug into setVoiceBank("/audio/voice/asena") and were tested with fakes only. Template-name and "Kurt yol gösteriyor…" lines have no placeholder (silent until recorded).

The live master limiter is a DynamicsCompressor, not a true-peak limiter: see runtimeChain for the stacked-effects worst case (same behaviour as the other games). Every rendered asset is below −1 dBTP.
Very short effects (paw, click, tick, coin) read under their momentary class target because they are shorter than the 400 ms window (same as the other sets).
Not verified: GitHub CI, a production (build:cloudflare) runtime, Safari/Firefox, mobile devices, and the game screen wiring (components/asena/** and the /game/asena screen are other agents' work).
